security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL implements debug/trace security controls using the old CSR name 'msdcfg' with old field names (SDEDBGALW, USEDBGALW, SDETRCALW, USETRCALW) and old bit positions (e.g., SDEDBGALW at bit 7, SDETRCALW at bit 8), while Rev 0.7.4 mandates a new dedicated CSR 'mdtcfg' at a different CSR address (TBD) with renamed fields (SEDBGALW, UEDBGALW, SETRCALW, UETRCALW) and a new bit layout [SEDBGALW:0, VSEDBGALW:1, UEDBGALW:2, WPRI:5, SETRCALW:8, VSETRCALW:9, UETRCALW:10, WPRI:21]. Additionally, if the RTL wires debug/trace security control logic to read from the old msdcfg CSR address while M-mode firmware writes to the new mdtcfg address per spec, the control fields would permanently read as 0 (reset value), causing all external debug and trace to be disallowed or controlled by stale/unreachable register state.
security_spec.summary: CSR renamed from msdcfg to mdtcfg with all field names changed (drop SD/US prefixes: SDEDBGALW→SEDBGALW, USEDBGALW→UEDBGALW, SDETRCALW→SETRCALW, USETRCALW→UETRCALW) and new bit layout; hardware implementing old names/addresses would have debug security controls mapped to wrong CSR, creating privilege escalation via unenforced debug access restrictions
